sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].

FY2026 was the sharpest step, revenue up 17.8% on growth in Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud driven by Azure and Productivity and Business Processes by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [D472][P17].
FY2024's 15.7% growth was driven by Gaming, where revenue rose 39% with 44 points of net impact from the Activision Blizzard acquisition [D364][P26].
The one stall was FY2023, when revenue grew 6.9% and operating income 6.2% as More Personal Computing fell 8.7% [D311][D312][D932].
Microsoft Cloud supplied 16.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth and reached 64.6% of revenue [D568][D472][D566].
Server products and cloud services added $31.0 billion, up 31%, driven by Azure and other cloud services, whose revenue grew 41% [P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services contributed 5.1pp of growth on 16.2% growth, while XBOX subtracted 0.6pp as revenue fell 7.1% [D649][D648][D713][D712].
The XBOX decline came from lower content and services and a 29% fall in hardware on fewer consoles sold [P10].
Operating income grew 20.8% against 17.8% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 53.3%, and operating costs grew 10.3pp slower than revenue [D473][D472][D498][D499].
Operating margin reached 46.8% in FY2026, a window high against a 41.7% median and 30.1% low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped to 67.9% from 69.8% in FY2024, below the 68.2% median, as cost of revenue took 0.9pp off operating margin [F30][F28][D981][D500].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
In FY2026 net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below the 46.8% operating margin, with other income of $10.7 billion and a 19.4% tax rate narrowing the gap [F70][F50][D1023][X124][D458].
Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income, in line with the 1.34x median, but free cash flow of $67.0 billion was only 0.50x, a window low [F100][D459][D1013][F120][D460][D988].
Cash from operations rose $46.8 billion primarily on higher cash received from customers and lower income tax payments [P1].
Capex reached 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x D&A, and free cash flow margin fell to 20.2% from a 30.3% median [D455][D461][D456][D984].
Investing cash use rose $66.9 billion, mainly a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions and $22.2 billion more for components [P1].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, or 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell to $40.3 billion while cash and investments held at $113.2 billion [D464][D463].
Buybacks and dividends of $48.7 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D467][D468][D493].
The cushion is real but thinner than it looks: net cash covers less than a year of the current capex run [D465][F110].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at 0.70x and 0.50x, the latter a window low [R1][D406][D460][D988].
This is capex, not earnings quality: operating cash flow conversion held at 1.37x, so the flag tracks the AI build rather than weakening collections [D459].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2017 though reported in FY2018, so cash and investments and net cash omit them that year [R6][X158].
Any FY2017-to-FY2018 liquidity comparison is therefore not like for like and should not carry a conclusion [R6].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers toward the 30.3% median from 20.2%, reported in the FY2027 10-K cash flow section [D984][D456].
Whether capex stays above the 34.9% of revenue reached in FY2026 or falls back toward the 22.9% of FY2025 [D455][D401].
Whether operating margin holds above the 41.7% median after reaching the 46.8% window high [D975][D974].
